name: Wattens
kurzbeschreibung: Home of Swarovski Kristallwelten – sparkling art worlds and industrial history in the Inntal.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The historic market town of Wattens is situated at 564 metres above sea level in the Lower Inn Valley south of the River Inn, roughly 15 kilometres east of the provincial capital Innsbruck within the Innsbruck-Land district. Home to approximately 8,100 residents, Wattens occupies the mouth of the scenic Watten Valley, serving as an internationally acclaimed centre of commerce, design, and industry. Global fame stems from crystal manufacturer Swarovski, which maintains its world headquarters here and operates Swarovski Crystal Worlds, one of Austria's top visitor attractions. In parallel, Wattens boasts an industrial heritage in specialty paper manufacturing dating back to 1559. The town uniquely blends avant-garde art installations and crystal splendour with alpine nature, industrial pioneering spirit, and prominent Iron Age archaeological excavations.

Geschichte

Human habitation at Wattens extends deep into antiquity: more than 2,500 years ago, the fortified Raetian hilltop settlement of Himmelreich thrived on a wooded ridge overlooking the valley. The settlement was first documented around 930 AD as 'Vuattanes', deriving from the Celtic personal name Vattanos. In 1559, Christoph Reitminner established North Tyrol's oldest paper mill along the rushing Wattenbach stream, evolving into today's world-leading specialty paper producer Wattenspapier. A historic watershed arrived in 1895 when Bohemian glass cutter Daniel Swarovski chose Wattens to harness the abundant hydroelectric energy of the mountain stream for his patented mechanical crystal-cutting machinery. The venerable parish church of St. Laurentius was rebuilt in neoclassical style following an 1809 fire, while the modern church of St. Mary was erected in 1958.

Anreise

Wattens enjoys first-class transport links within central Tyrol. Motorists reach the town directly via the Inntal Autobahn A12 at junction 61 (Wattens) or toll-free along the federal highway B171. Rail travelers benefit from frequent services at the Fritzens-Wattens railway station on the Lower Inn Valley line: S-Bahn Tirol trains (lines S4 and S5) and regional expresses provide rapid connections to Innsbruck Central Station in just 15 minutes. A modern pedestrian bridge spans the River Inn directly connecting the station platforms with the town centre. Furthermore, regular regional buses connect neighbouring villages, and a dedicated Swarovski Crystal Worlds shuttle bus operates multiple daily round trips directly from Innsbruck Central Station.

Tipps

The preeminent tourist attraction is Swarovski Crystal Worlds (Swarovski Kristallwelten): nestled beneath the iconic green head of the water-spouting Giant lie 18 subterranean Chambers of Wonder showcasing installations by renowned artists such as Yayoi Kusama, André Heller, and Salvador Dalí. In the 7.5-hectare landscaped garden, visitors marvel at the monumental Crystal Cloud containing more than 800,000 hand-set crystals reflected in a black mirror pool, an innovative four-storey play tower designed by Snøhetta, and a carousel by Jaime Hayon. History enthusiasts can explore the open-air archaeological site of the Raetian settlement Himmelreich, open year-round with preserved foundations. The award-winning Museum Wattens on the town square illuminates the interplay between prehistoric heritage, papermaking, and crystal craftsmanship.
